title: Approach to Elevated Troponin and Non‑Ischemic Myocardial Injury
summary: Elevated troponin indicates myocardial injury, not etiology. Distinguish acute myocardial infarction (MI) from acute/chronic non‑ischemic injury using symptoms, ECG, serial high‑sensitivity assays, and imaging. Management targets the cause (e.g., tachyarrhythmia, sepsis, myocarditis) rather than universal ACS therapy, which may harm when ischemia is absent.
clinicalQuestion: How should clinicians evaluate and manage patients with elevated troponin when type 1 MI is uncertain or unlikely?

heroStats.label: hs‑cTn rule‑out at 1–2 h
heroStats.value: NPV >99% for MI with ESC 0/1‑h or 0/2‑h pathways [1], [2]

heroStats.label: Type 2 MI mortality
heroStats.value: Higher 1‑yr mortality vs type 1 MI (adjusted HR ~1.5) [3]

heroStats.label: Myocarditis imaging
heroStats.value: CMR Lake Louise criteria sensitivity ~87%, specificity ~96% [4]

keyMoments.title: Troponin ≠ MI
keyMoments.body: High‑sensitivity troponin detects myocardial injury; **MI requires ischemia evidence** (symptoms, ECG, imaging) plus rise/fall in troponin [5].

keyMoments.title: Rapid Algorithms
keyMoments.body: Use **0/1‑h or 0/2‑h hs‑cTn** strategies with clinical assessment to safely rule out MI and reduce unnecessary admissions [1], [2].

keyMoments.title: Avoid Routine Antithrombotics
keyMoments.body: In non‑ischemic injury or type 2 MI, **treat the trigger**; routine heparin, P2Y12 inhibitors, or cath may be harmful without plaque rupture [6], [7].

keyMoments.title: ECG and Imaging Guide Etiology
keyMoments.body: New ST‑changes or regional wall‑motion abnormalities favor type 1 MI; diffuse ST‑elevation/PR‑depression suggests pericarditis; **CMR clarifies myocarditis/takotsubo** [4], [8].

keyMoments.title: Prognosis Matters
keyMoments.body: Elevated troponin in sepsis, PE, CKD, or HF predicts **higher mortality**; address underlying disease and optimize cardioprotection [3], [9], [10].

sections.title: Structured Approach to Elevated Troponin
sections.blurb: Differentiate acute MI, type 2 MI, and non‑ischemic myocardial injury using clinical context, ECG, serial hs‑cTn, and targeted imaging.

steps.title: Confirm an Acute Pattern
steps.body: Obtain baseline and repeat hs‑cTn at 1–2 h. **A rising/falling pattern plus ischemic evidence** supports acute MI; stable elevation suggests chronic injury (e.g., CKD) [1], [2], [5]. Use assay‑specific absolute deltas over relative change.

steps.title: Assess Ischemia Probability
steps.body: Integrate symptoms, risk factors, and ECG. **Typical ischemic symptoms or new ischemic ECG changes** increase pretest probability; atypical features (viral prodrome, pleuritic pain) point to non‑ischemic causes [5], [8].

steps.title: Apply Rapid Algorithms
steps.body: Use validated ESC **0/1‑h or 0/2‑h hs‑cTn** pathways for rule‑out/rule‑in. NPVs exceed **99%** for MI with appropriate cutoffs; combine with clinical judgment to avoid missed MI [1], [2].

steps.title: Targeted Imaging
steps.body: If uncertainty persists: bedside echo for regional wall‑motion abnormalities; if non‑ischemic suspected, **CMR** within 7 days improves diagnostic yield for myocarditis or takotsubo [4], [8]. Consider CT‑CA for low‑to‑intermediate risk chest pain without clear ECG changes [11].

steps.title: Classify the Etiology
steps.body: Use the **Fourth Universal Definition of MI** framework: type 1 MI (plaque rupture), type 2 MI (supply‑demand mismatch), or non‑ischemic myocardial injury (e.g., myocarditis, renal failure, sepsis) [5].

steps.title: Manage the Cause
steps.body: For type 1 MI: guideline‑directed ACS therapy. For type 2 MI or injury: **correct triggers** (hypoxemia, anemia, tachyarrhythmia, sepsis), optimize BP/O2, treat infection/PE, and avoid routine dual antiplatelet/anticoagulation unless another indication exists [6], [7], [9], [10].

sections.title: Practical Checklists
sections.blurb: Concise actions to reduce missed MI and overtreatment of non‑ischemic injury.

cards.title: Serial Testing
items: Repeat hs‑cTn at 1–2 h; use absolute deltas per assay [1], [2]
Obtain 12‑lead ECG at presentation and with symptoms
Trend vitals and oxygenation to identify supply–demand mismatch

cards.title: Key Labs
items: BNP/NT‑proBNP for HF context; D‑dimer if PE pretest warrants

cards.title: When to Image
items: POCUS/echo for wall‑motion, effusion, LV dysfunction
CMR within 7 days if myocarditis/takotsubo likely [4], [8]
CT‑coronary angiography for low–intermediate risk without clear ischemia [11]

cards.title: Avoid Harm
items: Do not default to heparin or DAPT without type 1 MI features [6], [7]
Avoid unnecessary catheterization in clear non‑ischemic injury
Dose‑adjust renally cleared drugs in CKD with chronic troponin elevation

cards.title: Prognostic Actions
items: Optimize guideline‑directed therapy for CAD/HF if present
Address triggers: control rate/rhythm, treat hypoxemia/sepsis, correct anemia
Arrange follow‑up; elevated troponin in sepsis/PE/CKD predicts worse outcomes [3], [9], [10]

cards.title: Documentation Pearls
items: State: acute vs chronic injury; MI type per Universal Definition [5]
Record delta troponin values and ECG/imaging corroboration
Specify identified trigger and treatment plan
